entry.title: Error KI100 during Vendor Condition Contract Settlement with Cross Company delivery
entry.content:
Hello,

I have one document with one single item that we sell to our client but procure from a different one - I sell from Germany but deliver out of Poland. My billing document is correctly posted to the partner profit center and we face no problem in the O2C process, but, when I try to run a settlement where this document is to be found I get the KI100 error because of the different CO account assignment - when we debug we see that we have the correct profit center (the partner profit center) in our settlement document to be created but still the system checks the other profit center for whatever reason I can't understand.

 

I don't think the option to have the message defined as warning would be the trick - what impact would it have on other processes? besides this I could not find anything at all that would be Condition Contract Settlement related and as mentioned outside CCS (we are still in ECC) everything works well.

--------------------------

has anyone an idea how to workaround in CCS so that it works??

 

 

Thanks in advance,

Paula.

entry.title: Use BDRs to bring legacy business volume into S4hana Condition Contracts
entry.content:
Hi All,

When going live mid-year with client tier-based quantity rebate agreements, a common requirement is migrating legacy business volume into S/4HANA to avoid manual off-system calculations for tier determination and final settlement.

I am considering the following technical approach:

 Legacy Volume Ingestion: Load legacy business volume into S/4HANA using Billing Document Requests (BDRs).

 Profile Configuration: Create an additional Business Volume Profile table specifically to capture these BDR document types.

 Additional Volume Assignment: Assign this new Business Volume Profile table as an "Additional Business Volume" source within the Business volume profile.

For anyone who has implemented this approach in a live environment:

 What technical, reporting, or performance issues did you encounter? Were there any specific edge cases with tier recalculations or scale thresholds during the first mid-year settlement?

Any insights, lessons learned, or alternative recommended practices would be greatly appreciated.

Regards

Hari

entry.title: ECC Rebate Agreement Migration to S/4HANA Private Cloud
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

We are currently working on a brownfield system conversion from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and are reviewing how to handle existing SD rebate agreements. In the SAP S/4HANA Simplification List, SAP states:

“In SAP S/4HANA, Settlement Management replaces SD Rebate Processing, which means that existing rebate agreements can only be processed up until the end of the validity date of the agreement and must then be closed by a final settlement. New agreements can only be created based on condition contracts. Therefore, the corresponding transaction codes VBO1 resp. VB(D for the creation of rebate agreements is not available anymore.”

I would like to understand exactly what SAP means by:

“Existing rebate agreements can only be processed up until the end of the validity date of the agreement.”

For example, if an ECC rebate agreement is still active and its validity period extends beyond the S/4HANA cutover date, Does the existing ECC rebate agreement remain available after the brownfield conversion to S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition? Can the existing agreement continue to accumulate/process rebate-relevant business volume in S/4HANA until its original validity end date?

I would appreciate clarification from anyone who has handled this in an ECC to S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition brownfield conversion, particularly regarding the actual settlement process for agreements that remain open across the cutover date.
